business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1 Business section.
business_model.claim: AII sells personal residential property insurance (homeowners, condominium, vacant dwellings, investment properties) to individual policyholders, predominantly in Florida, through its carrier subsidiary AIIC.
quotes: Through our insurance carrier subsidiary, American Integrity Insurance Company ("AIIC"), we provide personal residential property insurance for single- family homeowners and condominium owners, as well as coverage for vacant dwellings and investment properties, predominantly in Florida.

business_model.claim: Florida accounted for 93.7% of policies in-force and 96.5% of in-force premium as of December 31, 2025, making the company heavily concentrated in one state's property insurance market.
quotes: Florida represented 93.7% of our policies in-force as of December 31, 2025 and 96.5% of our in- force premium as of December 31, 2025.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A under 'Cost and Availability of Reinsurance.'
business_model.claim: AII cedes a large share of its gross premiums earned to reinsurers: 60.5% in the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 69.7% in the same period in 2025, meaning the company retains only a fraction of the risk it writes.
quotes: We ceded 60.5% and 69.7% of our gross premiums earned in the six months ended June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2025, respectively.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Business section and elaborated in the MD&A.
business_model.claim: Distribution is primarily through the Voluntary Market (independent agents, new-construction builder agents, and national carriers referring business), with a smaller share of policies assumed from Florida's Citizens Property Insurance Corporation.
quotes: we primarily distribute our products through the "Voluntary Market," meaning we directly underwrite and sell residential property insurance coverage to single family homeowners and condominium owners.

business_model.claim: As of December 31, 2025, 77.5% of in-force policies were from the Voluntary Market and 22.5% were assumed from Citizens.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, 77.5% of our in-force policies were from the Voluntary Market and 22.5% were assumed from Citizens.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Q2 2026 earnings press release (8-K EX-99.1).
business_model.claim: In Q2 2026 the company sold 43,000 voluntary new business policies, a record, up 54% year-over-year, and wrote 126,308 new and renewal voluntary-market policies, up 27.9% versus Q2 2025.
quotes: 43K voluntary new business policies sold in the quarter, a record for American Integrity, up 54% vs. the second quarter of 2025 and 44% vs. the first quarter of 2026
Wrote 126,308 new and renewal policies in the voluntary market, an increase of 27.9% compared to the second quarter of 2025

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A under 'Cost and Availability of Reinsurance – Quota share.'
business_model.claim: Effective January 1, 2026, the company reduced its quota-share ceding commission from 40% to 25%, which increases policy acquisition and G&A expenses because reinsurers reimburse less of those costs.
quotes: Effective January 1, 2026, we reduced the percentage of our ceding commission on our quota share reinsurance treaty from 40% to 25%, which impacted the comparability of our results between periods.

business_model.basis: Stated in both the 10-K MD&A and the 10-Q MD&A under 'Seasonality of our Business.'
business_model.claim: The company's results are highly seasonal because hurricanes and tropical storms typically occur between June 1 and November 30, and catastrophe reinsurance renews on June 1, causing Q2 ceded premiums to be substantially higher than other quarters.
quotes: Our financial results are highly seasonal due to the occurrence of hurricanes and tropical storms typically between June 1st and November 30th of each year in Florida and the other states in which we operate.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Q2 2026 earnings press release.
business_model.claim: In Q2 2026 the company renewed its catastrophe excess-of-loss reinsurance program with $3 billion of total third-party coverage at an estimated cost of $430–$440 million, with a risk-adjusted rate decrease at the upper end of 15–20% and a reduction in aggregate retention from $95 million to $75 million.
quotes: Renewed the Company's catastrophe excess of loss ("CAT XOL") reinsurance program effective June 1, 2026, providing $3 billion of total third-party catastrophe coverage at a total estimated cost of $430 - $440 million

The Company benefitted from the upper end of 15-20% CAT XOL risk-adjusted rate decreases, while retaining its 1-in-130 year probable maximum loss level and reducing its aggregate retention from $95 million to $75 million

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Business section and the 10-Q MD&A overview.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Business section under 'Our Business' and 'Our Competitive Strengths.'

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A as a key factor affecting results.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) citing U.S. Census Bureau data; the continuation condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Florida's population growth (23.4 million residents, second-fastest growth rate) expands the addressable residential property insurance market, and for this driver to continue, Florida's population and housing stock must keep growing and the market must not saturate.
quotes: Florida was the third most populous state in the United States, with 23.4 million residents as of July 1, 2025, and recorded the second fastest population growth rate of all states in the United States from 2024 to 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 (8-K earnings release) and P2 (10-K MD&A); the continuation condition is inferred from the distribution model described in P1.

quotes: 43K voluntary new business policies sold in the quarter, a record for American Integrity, up 54% vs. the second quarter of 2025 and 44% vs. the first quarter of 2026

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 (8-K) and P3 (10-Q MD&A); the 2024 and 2025 volumes are from P2 (10-K MD&A).

quotes: Assumed just 81 policies, as we determined that fewer policies from Citizens met our underwriting and targeted profitability standards
In 2026, we expect take-outs to be a smaller portion of our gross premiums written compared to 2024 and 2025.

Recent legislative changes, however, have improved operating conditions in the Florida insurance market, including a reduction in claims litigation activity since the reforms were enacted in December 2022.
